deltas.forward:
Index: docs/kit/02-api-reference.md
===================================================================
--- docs/kit/02-api-reference.md
+++ docs/kit/02-api-reference.md
@@ -260,7 +260,7 @@
 | `GET ledger/erasures` | The visitors whose erasure is pending, each with the moment of erasure: a warehouse job drops their rows at or before that moment from what it loads, until the nightly rewrite has removed them from the objects themselves. `ledger/batches` says how many are pending |
 | `POST ledger/erasures` `{ visitorId }` | The ledger half of an erasure: writes the tombstone every reader honours at once and empties the visitor's ring. The identity erase route calls the same function after erasing the profile. `POST ledger/erasures/rewrite` runs the nightly rewrite now |
 | `GET replay/{decision_id}` | Validates recorded page dependencies, loads required prefix archives (none for a genuine pin), and compares the target including authority/exploration: `{ equal, diff[], used }`; unavailable or inconsistent dependencies fail explicitly |
-| `POST learn/report` `{ date, brand?, policies? }` and `GET learn/report?date=&brand=` | Raw attribution diagnostics from available hour aggregates, or bounded day-ledger reads for custom policies/fallback. GET reads the stored day, not a guarantee of current or settled coverage. Additive `coverage` reports source limitations; legacy `hours` and counts remain compatible. Raw fallback/custom reads refuse past 800 ledger objects. Aggregation does not establish any-size capacity or complete history. No visitor id in the result |
+| `POST learn/report` `{ date, brand?, policies? }` and `GET learn/report?date=&brand=` | Raw attribution diagnostics from available hour aggregates, or bounded day-ledger reads for custom policies/fallback. Explicit `policies` arrays, including empty or preset-equivalent arrays, return response-only results and never save the canonical day. Omit `policies` for ordinary canonical publication. GET reads the stored canonical day, not a guarantee of current or settled coverage. Additive `coverage` reports source limitations; legacy `hours` and counts remain compatible. Raw fallback/custom reads refuse past 800 ledger objects. Aggregation does not establish any-size capacity or complete history. No visitor id in the result |
 | `GET learn/report/window?from=&to=&brand=` | Pools stored day diagnostics over at most 92 inclusive days. Missing reports and dated normalized coverage remain visible; no experimental inference or maturity claim |
 | `POST learn/cycle[?brand=]` | Unavailable: valid authenticated requests return 503. Automatic and on-demand proposal generation/application are withdrawn pending W29 safeguards |
 | `GET learn/proposals` | Read-only historical records, explicitly unverified; retained statuses are not proof of successful application and the returned history is not guaranteed complete |
@@ -272,6 +272,8 @@
 
 Report `coverage.version:1` preserves known missing/truncated hours, visitor uncertainty, hours whose persisted ring progress was not advanced, and each built hour's horizon (including zero or unknown). Unadvanced progress does not mean every displayed credit is wrong. `minHorizonMs` is null when contributing horizons or sources are missing/unknown; legacy `hours.horizonMs` describes the old last-hour value, never a minimum. Stored legacy or malformed metadata cannot establish coverage; known warnings survive read-time normalization without rewriting reports. Both operator views show these limits before empty results. Maturity is always `unknown`, and status is only `incomplete` or `unknown`: neither age nor an empty warning list establishes delivery completeness, compatible policies or experimental readiness. Direct ledger reports cannot establish carry-in history. This bounded JSON/view contract does not change CSV exports, repair history or certify external consumers.
 
+Custom report results remain usable in the POST response and the legacy UI's local CSV download, but reload GET/window reads the canonical saved report. This forward isolation does not detect or repair prior overwrites, certify old writers, resolve concurrent canonical publications or strengthen canonical write acknowledgements.
+
 W29 availability: stored `assisted`/`autonomous` configuration is retained but dormant; neither a stored mode nor an old client enables automation. The slots index's `autonomy` field describes stored configuration, and `learn/queue.proposals_pending` counts historical `proposed` statuses, not actionable work. Both consoles withdraw autonomy editing and proposal decisions. Safe autonomy remains an unmet delivery obligation, not a waived requirement.
 
 ## 6. Operators: sign-in and accounts
